stand_ins.label: STAND-IN A, optimistic: the Gata4 factor and depth ratio borrowed from the other replicate, scored on each replicate. Same knockout, so a replicate fold, which never counts under the adoption rule; it lacks s1's composition term (D8 measured that term at +0.22 and -0.43 points on top of the borrowed factor; gata4_decisions.json). It shows the factor carries between two runs of one knockout, which a processing effect shared by one run could explain (rules.yaml, the 2026-10-19 note that adds rule 6), not that it carries to another knockout.

STAND-IN B, the only cross-knockout reading of a per-gene factor: the Mab21l2 factor on WT E8.75 cells, scored on Gata4 (D11b, whose pre-registered bar is a board score of at least 60 on every target; it scored 59.40 on rep1, so it failed). A different factor from s1's, but the situation of the test: one knockout's factor applied to another knockout.

STAND-IN: wild-type cells with s2's five depleted states at depletion 0.5 (log2 1.0, against s2's 0.608, log2 0.718), no factor, scored on Gata4: the beta-catenin composition rule read on another knockout, written before any Gata4 file was opened (rules.yaml, A11).

caveats: Points left are measured to the split-half ceiling, which no prediction reaches, and the skill map is 1/(1 + x): halving a metric's remaining distance takes its skill from 0.5 to 0.667, so equal points left on two metrics do not mean equal reach.

Where an entry sits near the floor (the M1 and H1 stand-ins, T3's s2 stand-in), the ranking of points left mostly restates the weights: at the floor every metric leaves 50 x weight points, so the heaviest metric comes first (T1 mmd_u 0.30, T2 neighborhood_mmd 0.25, T3 de_score 0.30). On T2 the four groups weigh 0.25 each and neighborhood_mmd alone carries a whole group's weight, so the weakest metric is read for reference only and the weakest weighted component is the group (docs/PLAN.md section 3, item 9).

Where a board's counting backtests name different weakest groups, those groups count as tied, and so do gaps across boards that lie within the spread of a board's stand-ins (experiments/harness/TRIES.md rule 6); the per-task lines above show each backtest's own weakest group.

These are backtests on released transitions, not the test: T1 on E9.5 -> E10.5 (test E10.5 -> E12.5); the heart one and 1.75 days ahead (test two); the embryo at t = 1/3 and 2/3 (test 1/2). Each backtest's geometry, sampling and depth differ from the test's (TRIES.md diagnostics).

T1: the stand-in draws E9.5's own chamber mix (cardiomyocytes about 66% of heart cells) against E10.5's chamber-cut truth, while the test entry starts from E10.5's own mix, so mmd_u and the variogram here carry a composition mismatch the test entry does not carry in that form. B0 drawn to the truth's own chamber mix (an oracle base) scores 69.92 against that truth, against 49.68 for B0 at E9.5's mix (experiments/s2_hedge/README.md, t1-grid at 90b25d3, 10 seeds; a sensitivity analysis, not an adoption result). At test the open question is how E12.5's states and shares differ from E10.5's, which is where births by the legal route come in.
T1: the whole-E10.5 task is shown but not counted (a different tissue mix from the floor's); E8.5 -> E9.5 cannot run the entry.

T2 heart: the stand-in's shape and scale skills are a copy's (the reference stage's coordinates); the test entry's size comes from the pre-registered procedure, which no backtest scores, and sizes are closed to tries anyway.

T3: no row is an entry. Stand-in A is a replicate fold (one knockout, two runs), stand-in B a different factor; the composition magnitudes differ from the entries'. The harness rows on the counted folds are baseline rows only: wt_identity (the floor), our copy of WT cells and the organisers' shift_transfer.

The weights and the gate are the emulator's (src/vec/evaluate.py, gate floor_normalised). docs/PLAN.md section 1 says all three board formulas, the T2 gate included, were re-derived from over 1,000 public leaderboard rows to within 1e-4; the organisers have not published the gate's code.

This table chooses nothing: a change aimed at a weak component is registered in TRIES.md before its run and kept only under the adoption rule (docs/PLAN.md section 3, item 8) and TRIES.md rule 2; the data rules, the frozen s2 rules and the 2026-11-04 block stand.

definitions.skill: 0.5 = the published floor, 1 = the split-half ceiling; NaN counts as 0
definitions.gain: seed-paired mean of 100 x weight x (entry skill - baseline skill)
definitions.left: 100 x weight x (1 - entry skill); T2 shape terms: 100 x (0.25/3) x (1 - gate x skill)
definitions.gate: T2: min(1, 2 x skill(neighborhood_mmd)) per candidate and seed
definitions.weakest_group: the weakest weighted component: the scored group (src/vec/boards.py GROUPS id) with the most points left; ties at 0.01 points to the least gained over the floor (docs/PLAN.md section 3, item 9)
definitions.weakest_metric: the same rule over single metrics, for reference only
definitions.left_overall: points left x the board's weight in Overall (1 on T1 and T3, 0.5 on a T2 board)
